facts.ROLE-CODKIT: The Codkit repository is the distributable tool and does not contain a consumer fork's patch artifacts or product history.
facts.ROLE-PATCH-SET: The patch-set directory is a Git work tree that owns `codkit.json`, delta layers, cycle records, inventory, and review history.
facts.ROLE-FORK-TREE: The managed fork tree contains upstream VS Code history plus generated Codkit refs; direct human commits there are forbidden.

facts.FLOW-SYNC: `sync` materializes one patch-set revision over its configured upstream pin.
facts.FLOW-EDIT: Implementation work and upstream-run tests happen in the managed fork tree.
facts.FLOW-SAVE: `save` validates and serializes tree changes back into the patch set.
facts.FLOW-UPGRADE: An upgrade cycle advances the pin and records every resolution as patch-set history.
facts.FLOW-PUBLISH: `publish <patch-set-ref>` generates downstream refs from immutable patch-set and upstream coordinates.

facts.SELF-CONSISTENT-PATCHSET-COMMIT: Each patch-set commit is self-consistent: its pin, artifacts, inventory, and checks describe one reproducible result.
facts.NO-NEIGHBOUR-DEFAULT: There is no default sibling fork or patch-set directory.
facts.DISJOINT-ROOTS: The installed tool, patch-set directory, and fork directory are pairwise disjoint, including containment: a managed cleanup may never reach another root.
